sumInsured: Not specified in provided extract (Schedule of Benefits/Policy Schedule will specify Benefit-wise Sum Insured; illustration shows examples like ₹3,00,000)

good.name: PED Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of a pre-existing Disease (PED) and its direct complications shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy with insurer.
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases are not covered for the first 24 months of continuous coverage from the first policy start date. Claims for declared/known conditions will be payable only after this 2-year waiting period is completed.

good.name: Initial Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the first policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident
good.explanation: Illness-related treatment is not covered in the first 30 days from the policy commencement date, except if it is due to an accident. This is a standard waiting period and can affect claims soon after buying the policy.

good.name: Specific Illness Waiting
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of the listed Conditions, surgeries/treatments shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage
good.reference: Section 4.1(i)(b) Specific waiting period – code – Excl02
good.explanation: Treatment for the listed diseases/procedures is not covered for the first 24 months of continuous coverage. Claims for these conditions will be payable only after completing this 2-year waiting period.

good.name: Restore Benefit
good.quote: Benefit 7 : Recharge of Sum Insured... The Recharge shall be available only for all future Claims and not in relation to any Illness or Injury for which a Claim has already been admitted for that Insured Person during that Policy Year.
good.explanation: A recharge of Sum Insured is available only for future claims and cannot be used for the same illness/injury for which a claim has already been admitted in that policy year. This helps when Sum Insured is exhausted, but only for new conditions in the same year.

good.name: Consumables Allowance
good.quote: Benefit 2 : Consumable Allowance... The Company will pay the amount specified against this Benefit in the Schedule of Benefits for each continuous and completed period of 24 hours of Hospitalization
good.explanation: A fixed consumables allowance is paid for each continuous and completed 24 hours of hospitalization, as per the Schedule of Benefits. This can offset some non-medical item costs, but may not match actual hospital billing.

bad.name: Room Rent
bad.quote: Room Rent = 1% of Benefit 1 Sum Insured as specified in the Schedule of Benefits per day of Hospitalization.
bad.explanation: Room rent is limited to 1% of Benefit 1 Sum Insured per day as per the Schedule of Benefits. Choosing a higher category room can lead to large out-of-pocket costs and may also trigger proportionate deductions.

bad.name: Proportionate Deduction
bad.quote: then the Policyholder/ Insured Person shall bear the ratable proportion of the total Associate Medical Expenses... in the proportion of the difference between the Room Rent actually incurred and the Room Rent specified in the Policy Schedule
bad.explanation: If you stay in a room that costs more than your eligible room rent, you must bear a proportionate share of associated medical expenses (not just the room rent). This can significantly reduce the claim payout even when other bills are otherwise admissible.

bad.name: Co-pay
bad.quote: Co-payment is applicable on all the Benefits / Optional Covers except Benefit 2, Benefit 3, Benefit 5, Benefit 7, Benefit 9, Optional Cover 2 & Optional Cover 3.
bad.reference: Section 3. Benefits Covered Under The Policy – General Conditions applicable to all Benefits, clause (f)
bad.explanation: A co-payment applies on most benefits/optional covers, with only the listed benefits excluded from co-pay. This means you will pay a percentage of each admissible claim (as per the schedule), reducing the insurer’s payout.

bad.name: Disease Sub-limits
bad.quote: The Company will indemnify... in respect of the below mentioned Ailments / Procedures up to the amount specified against each and every Ailment / Procedure mentioned in the Policy Schedule
bad.reference: Section 3.1.1(c)(iii) Expenses incurred on treatment for Named Ailments / Procedures
bad.explanation: Specific named ailments/procedures are payable only up to the rupee amount shown in the Policy Schedule. Even with a high Sum Insured, these sub-limits can cap payouts for common treatments.

bad.name: Modern Treatments
bad.quote: Expenses related to any kind of Advance Technology Methods other than mentioned in the Clause 3.1.1 (d).
bad.explanation: Advanced technology methods are excluded unless they are specifically listed under Clause 3.1.1(d). This can lead to claim rejections for newer procedures not explicitly covered in the wording.

bad.name: Non-medical Expenses
bad.quote: Annexure II - List of Expenses Generally Excluded ("Non-medical")... Gloves... Mask... Nebulisation Kit... Any Kit With No Details Mentioned
bad.reference: Annexure II - List of Expenses Generally Excluded (Non-medical)
bad.explanation: Many commonly billed hospital items (like gloves, masks, nebulisation kits, and unspecified kits) are listed as generally excluded non-medical expenses. These costs can become out-of-pocket unless covered through a specific allowance/benefit.

unclear.name: Pre-hospitalization Cover
unclear.quote: The Company will indemnify the Medical Expenses up to the amount specified against this Benefit in the Schedule of Benefits... As Pre-hospitalization Medical Expenses immediately prior... As Post-hospitalization Medical Expenses immediately following... provided that the Company shall not be liable... for any Post-hospitalization Medical Expenses that were incurred 30 days or more after the Policy End Date
unclear.explanation: Pre- and post-hospitalization medical expenses are covered, but the exact day limits/amounts are as per the Schedule of Benefits and are not stated here. Post-hospitalization expenses incurred 30 days or more after the Policy End Date are not payable.
